z00188.d: A simple march in C from Sor's guitar method, using straightforward rhythms and chord shapes. Practises steady pulse and clean fingerstyle at an early stage.

z00189.d: Guitar arrangement of Tchaikovsky's gentle dreamy piece from the Album for the Young, with a singing melody over soft chords. Trains tone, legato and phrase shaping.

z00190.d: Arranged Gavotte from Bach's sixth cello suite: a bright, bouncy D major dance with the characteristic half-bar upbeat. Practises crisp articulation and a clear two-part texture.

z00191.d: Lively first Bourrée from the third cello suite in G, arranged for guitar. Practises quick fingerwork, steady duple rhythm and clear articulation.

z00192.d: Slow, stately dance in triple time from Bach's third suite, with a weighty second-beat emphasis. Practises sustained tone, chordal playing and ornamented expression.

z00193.d: Melancholy lyrical piece in minor by Napoléon Coste, with a singing line over an arpeggiated accompaniment. Practises tone, fingerstyle arpeggios and expressive shaping.

z00194.d: A slow, expressive Andantino from Sor's method with a flowing melody and arpeggiated support. Practises legato line, voice-leading and tonal control.

z00195.rw: Good contrast of minor and major

z00196.d: Fast study in A minor by Carcassi built on rolling arpeggios across the strings. Develops right-hand fluency, evenness and speed with a clear musical shape.

z00197.d: Lively military quick-march by Coste, with crisp rhythms and bright chords. Practises precise rhythm, clean chord changes and energetic articulation.

z00198.d: Prelude from Bach's second cello suite in A minor: a restless, flowing piece with sweeping arpeggios and dramatic chords. Demands polyphonic clarity, stamina and a strong sense of line.

z00199.d: Cheerful and playful Giocoso by Mauro Giuliani, fast and light with arpeggiated figures and scales. Practises agility, evenness and clean chord changes.

z00393.d: Easy duet exercise from Sor's progressive Op. 35 studies, with the student playing a simple part against the teacher's. Practises steady pulse, clean notes and listening in ensemble.

z00394.d: Simple duet arrangement of the first piece in Schumann's Album for the Young, a gentle melody. Practises smooth tone, steady rhythm and ensemble listening.

z00395.d: Short, lilting waltz from Carulli's guitar method. Practises steady triple time, simple chord accompaniment and light, clear melody.

z00396.d: Gentle Andantino from Giuliani's studies, with a flowing melody over an arpeggiated accompaniment. Practises right-hand arpeggio control and singing tone.

z00397.d: Short study in C from Sor's lessons, with a regular broken-chord pattern. Practises right-hand fluency, clean left-hand changes and balanced melody and bass.

z00398.d: Elegant mazurka from a set of easy pieces by an Argentine guitarist. Practises mazurka rhythms, expressive melody and simple chord textures in Romantic style.

z00399.d: Lively, spirited Bourrée from the Bach Lute Suite in E minor, a guitar favourite. Practises crisp rhythm, clear two-part texture and light, buoyant phrasing.

z00400.d: Slow, stately Sarabande from the B minor violin partita, arranged for guitar. Practises sustained chords, expressive ornamentation and voice-leading in a dignified triple time.

z00401.d: Famous flowing G major prelude from the first cello suite, arranged for guitar. Practises even arpeggios, smooth harmonic shaping and long-range control.

z00402.d: Brisk Bourrée from the lute version of the E major violin partita, arranged for guitar. Practises rhythmic spring, clean polyphony and bright, clear articulation.

z00403.d: Fast, fugal Gigue from Bach's lute suite BWV 997, arranged for guitar. Practises quick imitative lines, rhythmic drive and clear voice separation.

z00404.d: Tárrega's famous concert waltz with a cheerful, memorable main tune, lyrical episodes and brisk passagework. Practises rubato within dance rhythm and balance of melody and chords.
